Done. Both stores updated.

Summary of what I learned and saved:

The miss was a clean ~4.19x factor with the correct sign (-131.4 vs gold -550.3). That signature — a single clean multiplicative miss, not a 2x rounding issue, with the sign right — means the CPI inflation arithmetic was fine and I read the wrong row: a partial/component balance instead of the Unemployment Trust Fund's all-accounts GRAND-TOTAL balance.

Generalizable lessons recorded:
- Patched the officeqa-treasury-bulletin skill with a new subsection under the CPI-adjust wrapper covering trust-fund total-balance questions: read the grand-total fund balance (not a state/railroad/federal sub-account), use December CPI of each year, and the diagnostic that a clean-factor miss with correct sign = wrong partial row.
- Noted that an inflation-adjusted signed difference can legitimately be NEGATIVE even when the fund grew nominally (inflating the earlier year up can exceed the later nominal value).
- Compacted the memory note to extend "TOTAL currency = grand total" to trust-fund "total balance" too.

This generalizes to any trust-fund "total balance" CPI-adjust question in the dataset.
